question: In the context of nutrients, the terms ‘tyrosine’, ‘glycine’ and ‘ornithine’ are types of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**amino acids. **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the context of nutrients, the terms** ‘tyrosine’, ‘glycine’ and ‘ornithine’** are types of **Amino acids.**
 
• Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins.
 
• More than 300 amino acids exist in nature but only **20 amino acids form proteins.**
 
• The 20 amino acids are called 20 alphabets of** bioprotein language.**
 
• 20 types of amino acids form protein, protein is a **heteropolymer**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Types of Amino Acids
 
• Nonessential amino acids: These amino acids are produced naturally by the body and don’t matter the food you are having.
 
 
• The following are examples of nonessential amino acids:
 
• Alanine
 
• Asparagine
 
• Aspartic acid
 
• Glutamic acid
 
 
 
• Essential amino acids: These amino acids come from the food we eat. it can't be produced by the body.
 
• The following are essential amino acids:
 
 
• Histidine
 
• Isoleucine
 
• Leucine
 
• Lysine
 
• Methionine
 
• Phenylalanine
 
• Threonine
 
• Tryptophan
 
• Valine
 
 
 
• Conditional amino acids: These are usually not essential to everyday living but are important when you're sick, injured, or stressed.
 
• The following are Conditional amino acids :
 
 
• Arginine
 
• Cysteine
 
• Glutamine
 
• **Tyrosine**
 
• **Glycine**
 
• **Ornithine**
 
• Proline
 
• Serine
